introTitle: Help number New York’s subway exits
introBody: We’re asking New Yorkers and subway riders to create a proposed exit numbering system together. Throughout 2027, you’ll vote on small groups of stations across the NYC Subway and Staten Island Railway. When voting concludes, we plan to present the results to the MTA.
instructions: Select an exit. Give it a number.
instructionBody: Use each number once. There’s no right answer — choose the order that makes sense to you.
mapHelp: Tap a marker, or use the exit list.
listHelp: Choose a number for each location. You can change it anytime before submitting.
saved: Draft saved on this browser when local storage is available.
reviewHelp: Check your proposed numbers before submitting your ballot.
submitError: We couldn’t submit this ballot. Please check every station and try again.
thanksBody: Thank you for taking the time to number these exits. Your choices are saved in this browser.
archiveIntro: Explore the exit numbering arrangements from previous voting periods.
lifelong: But I’ve lived here my whole life…
disclaimer: The Exit Project is an independent civic project. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by the Metropolitan Transportation Authority.
footerNote: A little more clarity at street level.

pages.about: The Exit Project aims to crowdsource proposed numbers for exits throughout the NYC Subway and Staten Island Railway during 2027, then present the proposal to the MTA. Numbers would supplement street descriptions. These are not official MTA designations. Station data, mapping technology, the voting schedule and public infrastructure remain undecided.
pages.lifelong: Knowing your own station is a wonderful thing. Knowing every station is a bigger ask. Numbered exits would supplement geographic descriptions: “Exit 2 · NW corner of Broadway & 168th St.” The corner stays; the number adds shorthand for visitors, new arrivals, businesses giving directions and New Yorkers exploring an unfamiliar neighborhood. This example is explanatory, not an official exit designation.
pages.feedback: Feedback collection will be added before public voting. For now, note what felt confusing, what worked well and any accessibility issues you encountered.
pages.privacy: No account is required. Language, appearance, introduction dismissals and ballot drafts are stored in this browser when local storage is available. Ballots currently remain on your device. No analytics or advertising trackers are included. Clear this site’s browser data to remove saved preferences and drafts.
pages.terms: The Exit Project is an independent civic project. Proposed numbers do not change official station signage. The public voting terms and methodology will be established before launch.
pages.updates: Version 0.1 · Exit numbering with synchronized map and list controls, English and Korean, appearance settings and ballot review.

questions.a: An independent effort to propose useful exit numbers alongside existing geographic descriptions.
Assign every number from 1 to the station’s exit count exactly once, complete all stations, then review your ballot.

questions.q: How will the winning arrangement be selected?
questions.a: The aggregation method and tie handling are still to be decided.

questions.q: Where do the station exits come from?
questions.a: The source of station and exit data will be confirmed before public voting begins.
The plan is to complete the project by the end of 2027. The actual voting periods remain undecided.
A short number can make meeting up and giving directions easier while retaining street and corner descriptions.

questions.q: Will the MTA adopt these numbers?
questions.a: We plan to present the community proposal to the MTA. Adoption is not guaranteed and this project is not affiliated with the agency.
